input.subject: Smoke alarm still not refitted – 26 Tallowmere Close (ref NBL-016 / R/016)
input.body:
Dear Mr Vale,

Re: 26 Tallowmere Close, Fenbarrow, ZZ1 1ZZ – smoke alarm (ref NBL-016 / R/016)

We still have no confirmation that the smoke alarm has been refitted and tested. Our latest information from the tenant is that a fitter attended around 31 August, removed the old bracket, and could not refit the alarm because there was no bracket in the box, so the alarm is still not mounted.

The tenant also reported that on Saturday 20 September an unannounced person called at the property saying they were there to check something. They could not confirm who it was and did not let them in.

Please could you reply with:
1. the name and company of the electrician you have instructed, and whether they or anyone else on your behalf called at the property on Saturday 20 September;
2. when the alarm will be refitted and tested.

The tenant has recently been unwell, so we ask that any visit is arranged through us with notice in advance rather than by calling unannounced. Once you send us the electrician's details, we will coordinate access.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team, Northbridge Lettings

data.reasoning: I'll message the landlord asking for electrician details, whether a visit was sent, and the completion date, marking this high priority and logging the facts. Since the tenant asked to be left alone despite initiating contact on 20 Sep, I'll leave responding to them to a human rather than messaging directly.

input.summary: 26 Tallowmere Close (NBL-016). The tenant (Elise Rowan) reported on 7 Aug that the smoke alarm had come down. The landlord (Ronan Vale) said he would use his own electrician (ev 4, 7) and promised it would be done by the weekend after 12 Aug. A fitter attended around 31 Aug, removed the bracket and could not refit the alarm because there was no bracket in the box (ev 10). The alarm is still unmounted. The tenant was in hospital 5–11 Sep and on 11 Sep asked the agency to stop contacting them for now (ev 13). Contact was paused (ev 14). On 20 Sep the tenant called to report an unannounced person at the door claiming to 'check something'. They did not let them in (ev 15). The tenant says another agency contact passed this to building management (ev 16), but nothing has been verified. Today I emailed the landlord asking for the electrician's name and company, whether he sent Saturday's visitor, and a refit date, and asked that future visits go through us with notice.
input.checked: All 17 events. No contractor on the ticket, no attachments, no approvals, no holds, no property history or profile facts. Jev classified ev 15 as new_issue / review, safety_concern 0.72, needs_human_response 0.87. No lessons on record.

input.recommendation: Property manager (Maya Chen / Dorian Pike): 1) Look into the visitor report internally (which colleague, which building-management contact) and send the tenant one short, sensitive message, by email as they prefer, saying whether the visitor has been identified. Repeat their right to refuse unverified callers. 2) If the landlord doesn't give the electrician's details and a date within 2 days, consider an agency-arranged electrician. A working smoke alarm is a landlord compliance duty, and leaving it this long with a vulnerable tenant is a risk. Get the landlord's agreement or rely on compliance authority. 3) Consider offering a temporary battery smoke alarm in the meantime, delivered by appointment only.

result.summary: The smoke alarm at 26 Tallowmere Close has been unmounted for about 6 weeks. The landlord said he would use his own electrician, but we have no confirmation it's done. The tenant is recovering from a hospital stay and has asked for limited contact. They also reported an unannounced visitor nobody has identified. I emailed the landlord asking for the electrician's details, whether he sent the visitor, and a refit date. I escalated to a human at high priority and put a 2-day hold on the landlord. I did not contact the tenant, at their request.

judgement.why_this_decision: A missing smoke alarm is a fire-safety and compliance risk, and it has gone on for weeks (ev 10–14). The tenant is vulnerable after a hospital stay and has asked for less contact (ev 13), so tenant messages need a person's judgement. The visitor report (ev 15–16) is unverified and could be a security problem. Jev rated it review, with safety concern at 0.72. The landlord can answer who the electrician is, whether he sent the visitor and when the alarm will be fixed, so I asked him directly. The safety, vulnerability and visitor questions need agency judgement, so I escalated at high priority.
